reasoning: There were no wrong-to-right changes, and the persistent failures were largely unchanged. The prior verified-delta guidance remains useful, but did not resolve endpoint/action mismatches or missing scope. The two regressions expose schema risks: Booking.com’s optional language_code was moved to required, while the politician call gained an unsupported required limit and used lowercase federal instead of the canonical Federal. Other failures point to distinctions the edits should make clearer: CNN news versus CNN Arabic, COVID statistics versus news, broad location search versus car-location search, and API-specific canonical values such as amazon.de mapping to de.
meta_skill_content: Future optimizer: keep edits evidence-based and small, but address repeated failures rather than merely preserving the current skill. For every proposed change, check the exact endpoint, parameter names, required/optional grouping, canonical value and serialization against the tool schema and trace; never add arbitrary limits or move optional fields into required. Prioritize rules that distinguish actions and result types (e.g., news vs. statistics; a source’s latest news vs. its Arabic feed) and select the documented broad/configurable endpoint when it fits better than a narrower adjacent one. Make canonicalization endpoint-specific, not a copy of the user’s surface wording (e.g., hostname to documented marketplace code; publisher name to documented domain). Preserve coverage of every explicit target, scope, count, page, and mode; for comprehensive requests, permit multiple calls only when they cover distinct documented checks, not merely overlapping tools. Before accepting edits, regression-check stable cases so explicit qualifiers are not stripped and validated parameter groups remain intact.
